description: 100 questions on OOP classes and objects (coding and logic based, intermediate level)

questions.question: What keyword is used to define a class in Python?
questions.answer: class (e.g., class Dog:)

questions.question: What does `class Dog: pass` create?
questions.answer: An empty class named Dog that can be instantiated

questions.question: How do you create an object from the class Dog?
questions.answer: obj = Dog() (calling the class with parentheses)

questions.question: What does print(type(Dog())) output?
questions.answer: <class '__main__.Dog'>

questions.question: What does isinstance(Dog(), Dog) return?
questions.answer: True

questions.question: What does type(Dog()) == Dog return?
questions.answer: True (type gives the exact class)

questions.question: What does id(Dog()) == id(Dog()) return?
questions.answer: Usually False because the two instances are separate objects

questions.question: What does (lambda a, b: a is b)(Dog(), Dog()) return?
questions.answer: False (two calls create two distinct objects)

questions.question: What does a = Dog(); b = a; print(a is b) output?
questions.answer: True (b is a reference to the same object)

questions.question: What does a = Dog(); b = Dog(); print(a == b) output by default?
questions.answer: False (default equality is identity-based)

questions.question: When does __init__ get called?
questions.answer: Automatically, once, each time the class is instantiated

questions.question: class P: def __init__(self, name): self.name = name. What does P() do?
questions.answer: Raises TypeError: __init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'

questions.question: class P: def __init__(self, x=5): self.x = x. What does P().x return?
questions.answer: 5 (default used)

questions.question: class P: def __init__(self, x, y): self.x=x; self.y=y. How do you create it with keyword args?
class P: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. What does P().x return?
class P: pass. Can you create P() without defining __init__?
questions.answer: Yes; a default object.__init__ is used

questions.question: class P: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. Is self.x set for every instance?
questions.answer: Yes, __init__ runs for every instance and sets self.x

questions.question: class P: def set(self, v): self.v = v. What does p.v raise before set() is called?
questions.answer: AttributeError: 'P' object has no attribute 'v'

questions.question: class P: def set(self, v): self.v = v. p = P(); p.set(10); print(p.v) outputs?
questions.answer: 10 (attributes can be created in any method)

questions.question: Can you add a brand-new attribute to an object after creation, like p.color = 'red'?
questions.answer: Yes, Python objects allow dynamic attribute assignment

questions.question: What does p.missing raise when accessing an attribute that doesn't exist?
questions.answer: AttributeError

questions.question: What does getattr(p, 'x', 'nope') return when p has no x?
questions.answer: 'nope' (the default)

questions.question: What does hasattr(p, 'x') return when p has an x attribute?
questions.answer: True

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. What does A().hi() return?
questions.answer: 'hi'

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. What does A.hi(A()) return?
questions.answer: 'hi' (explicitly passing the instance as self)

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. What does A.hi() raise?
questions.answer: TypeError: hi() missing 1 required positional argument: 'self'

questions.question: inside an instance method, what does self refer to?
questions.answer: The exact object on which the method was called

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return self is A(). Is `self` bound when called as obj.m()` yes or no?
questions.answer: Yes, obj is passed automatically as self

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 42. What does A().m() return (no print)?
class A: def m(self): pass. What does A().m() return?
questions.answer: None (no return statement)

questions.question: class A: x = 10. What does A.x return?
questions.answer: 10 (class attribute read via the class)

questions.question: class A: x = 10. What does A().x return?
questions.answer: 10 (instance can read the class attribute)

questions.question: class A: x = []. a=A(); b=A(); a.x.append(1); print(b.x) outputs?
questions.answer: [1] (mutable class attribute is shared)

questions.question: class A: x = 10. a=A(); a.x = 5; print(A().x) outputs?
questions.answer: 10 (assigning on the instance only shadows it)

questions.question: class A: x = 10. a=A(); a.x = 5; print(a.x) outputs?
questions.answer: 5 (instance attribute shadows the class attribute)

questions.question: class A: x = 10. a=A(); a.x = 5; del a.x; print(a.x) outputs?
questions.answer: 10 (deleting the instance attribute re-exposes the class one)

questions.question: What does every instance's `__dict__` contain?
questions.answer: A dict of only its instance attributes, e.g., {'x': 5}

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. print(A().__dict__) outputs?
class A: pass. a=A(); a.x=1. print(a.__dict__) outputs?
Do methods appear in the instance's __dict__?
questions.answer: No, methods live on the class; the instance __dict__ holds only data

questions.question: What does dir(obj) return?
questions.answer: A sorted list of attribute/method names, including dunder methods

questions.question: class A: pass. print(len([1 for m in dir(A()) if m == 'bark'])) outputs?
questions.answer: 0 (no such method)

questions.question: What does object() create?
questions.answer: The simplest Python object with no instance attributes

questions.question: What does isinstance(Dog(), object) return?
questions.answer: True (every class ultimately inherits from object)

questions.question: class A: pass. What does bool(A()) return by default?
questions.answer: True (objects are truthy unless __bool__/__len__ says otherwise)

questions.question: What does print(A()) output when A has no __str__ or __repr__?
questions.answer: <__main__.A object at 0x...> (default object representation)

questions.question: class A: def __str__(self): return 'hello'. print(A()) outputs?
questions.answer: hello

questions.question: class A: def __repr__(self): return 'A()'. print(A()) outputs?
questions.answer: A() (repr used when __str__ is absent)

questions.question: What does type(A())() do for class A with no required args?
questions.answer: Creates a brand-new A instance via the class object itself

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. print(type(A().hi)) outputs?
questions.answer: <class 'method'> (a bound method)

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. print(A().hi is A().hi) outputs?
questions.answer: False (each access creates a new bound method object)

questions.question: What does callable(A().hi) return?
questions.answer: True (bound methods are callable)

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. What does callable(A.hi) return?
questions.answer: True (functions are callable)

questions.question: How many times does __init__ run for `[A() for _ in range(3)]`?
questions.answer: Three times, once per object

questions.question: class A: count = 0; def __init__(self): A.count += 1. After [A() for _ in range(5)], what is A.count?
class A: def __init__(self): self.n = 0. a=A(); a.n += 5; print(A().n) outputs?
questions.answer: 0 (instances are independent)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self, v): self.v = v. a=A(1); b=A(1); print(a.v == b.v) outputs?
questions.answer: True (values equal, though objects differ)

questions.question: What does `A is A` return for any class A?
questions.answer: True (the class object is a singleton in memory)

questions.question: What does A.__name__ return for class A?
questions.answer: 'A' (the class's name as a string)

questions.question: What does type(A()).__name__ return for class A?
Can a class method have any name as the first parameter instead of self?
questions.answer: Yes, but self is the strong convention

questions.question: class A: def m(this): return this. What does A().m() return?
questions.answer: The instance itself (first param name is arbitrary)

questions.question: What happens if a class method raises an exception during instantiation?
questions.answer: The exception propagates; no object is returned

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): raise ValueError('bad'). What does A() do?
questions.answer: Raises ValueError('bad'); construction fails

questions.question: What distinguishes one instance from another internally?
questions.answer: Different memory addresses/identity, reflected by different id()

questions.question: class A: x = 1. print(A.x is A().x) outputs?
questions.answer: True (read-only access returns the same class object value)

questions.question: What does hash(obj) return by default for a user object?
questions.answer: An identity-derived integer, stable while the object lives

questions.question: class A: pass. a=A(); b=a; print(id(a) == id(b)) outputs?
questions.answer: True (b aliases a)

questions.question: class A: pass. a=A(); print(id(a) == id(A())) outputs?
questions.answer: False (distinct objects) unless the first is already garbage collected

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return self. Can you call A.m(a) where a is an instance?
questions.answer: Yes, it works exactly like a.m()

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return self.m() causes what?
questions.answer: Infinite recursion (RecursionError) since m keeps calling itself

questions.question: Can two different classes define methods with the same name?
questions.answer: Yes; methods belong to their own class

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 1. class B: def m(self): return 2. print(A().m(), B().m()) outputs?
How do you detect the runtime class of an object in code?
questions.answer: type(obj) for the exact class, or isinstance(obj, Class) for matching

questions.question: class A: def f(self, x, y=10): return x + y. print(A().f(5)) outputs?
class A: def f(self, *a): return sum(a). print(A().f(1,2,3)) outputs?
What happens when you instantiate with too many args, e.g. P(1,2) when __init__ takes one?
questions.answer: TypeError: __init__() takes ... positional arguments but ... were given

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self, *args): print(len(args)). What does A(1,2,3) print inside __init__?
What does `A` (without parentheses) refer to?
questions.answer: The class object itself, not an instance

questions.question: Does defining a class execute its body?
questions.answer: Yes, the class body runs when the class statement executes, defining members

questions.question: class A: print('ran') ; When does 'ran' print?
questions.answer: Once, when the class definition itself is executed

questions.question: class A: x = 1 + 1. What is A.x?
How are instances stored: by value or by reference?
questions.answer: By reference; variables hold a reference to the same object

questions.question: What does [-1] do on p = P() when P has no __getitem__?
questions.answer: TypeError: 'P' object is not subscriptable

questions.question: class A: def __getitem__(self, i): return i * 2. What does A()[5] return?
class A: def __len__(self): return 7. print(len(A())) outputs?
class A: def __eq__(self, o): return True. print(A() == A()) outputs?
questions.answer: True (custom equality)

questions.question: class A: pass. print(A() == A()) outputs by default?
questions.answer: False (identity comparison)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self, v): self.v = v. How do you compare two A instances by v?
questions.answer: Compare attributes: a.v == b.v, or implement __eq__

questions.question: Is a class mutable at runtime?
questions.answer: Yes, you can add attributes/methods to a class after definition

questions.question: class A: pass; A.new_method = lambda self: 1. What does A().new_method() return?
questions.answer: 1 (methods can be attached at runtime)

questions.question: What does object.__new__ do during instantiation?
questions.answer: Allocates and returns the new instance before __init__ runs

questions.question: What order do __new__ and __init__ run when creating an object?
questions.answer: __new__ first (creates instance), then __init__ (initializes it)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 10. print(sorted(A().__dict__.keys())) outputs?
class A: def __init__(self): self.a = 1; self.b = 2. print(len(A().__dict__)) outputs?
What does print(type)(A()) or `type(A()) is A` evaluate to?
questions.answer: True (type of an instance is its class)

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 'm'. What does 'm' in dir(A()) return?
questions.answer: True

questions.question: class A: x = 5. What does 'x' in A.__dict__ return?
questions.answer: True

questions.question: What does 'x' in A().__dict__ return when x is only a class attribute?
questions.answer: False (instance dict does not copy class attributes)

questions.question: class A: pass; a=A(); a.x=1. After del a.x, what does 'x' in a.__dict__ return?
questions.answer: False (attribute deleted)
